BUYER GUIDE / BY KUMAR SAURABH MISHRA

Price starts with scope.

A useful quote separates the project from the services that continue after launch.

By Kumar Saurabh Mishra, founder of SiteSutra. Planning examples are original demonstrations.

Project fees

Page complexity, original design, content work, integrations, migration and testing all affect effort. Request a tailored quote with explicit deliverables rather than comparing headline prices alone.

Recurring costs

Hosting, domains, software licences and maintenance may recur. Ask who pays, what renews, and who owns the accounts. Advertising spend is separate from website and campaign-management fees.

Changes and support

Agree how additional work is priced and what launch support covers. Keep optional maintenance separate so you can compare proposals fairly.

Compare two hypothetical quotes fairly

Example only: Quote A covers four pages using supplied copy and one external booking link. Quote B covers the same pages plus copy development, legacy URL migration and an embedded booking journey. Compare the line items and exclusions before deciding which offers better value; no sample price or budget is asserted.

A useful commercial breakdown

Separate discovery/design/build/testing, migration, integrations and handover from domains, hosting, provider subscriptions and optional maintenance. Specify currency, applicable tax treatment, payment milestones, revisions and change approval in the actual proposal.

Turn uncertainty into a brief

If your budget is undecided, say so. Agree a minimum useful scope and optional later work. Download the scope tools or request a tailored website quote.
